Hollow Knight is a masterpiece, Silksong is just miserable. It's not the difficulty, it's the tone. Everything is more grotesque, baroque and overwrought than the last game, from art to story, NPCs and biomes have all had a significant charisma downgrade, to the point where I no longer care about exploring, because every area is just another boring slog with little sense of wonder or mystery. HK had a big infusion of the Studio Ghibli magic, and that's almost all gone in this sequel. I have never put so much time into a game I enjoyed so little.

What's left is a masochistic slog, with a downgraded gamefeel in the character to increase the difficulty of  combat. While Hornet is technically more mobile, the jump and basic attack have been mildly nerfed which means more precise timing and movement are required for all things. The game is harder and just feels noticeably worse than HK for the minute to minute gameplay, like a shoe that just slightly doesn't fit. Is the justification for this significantly more interesting challengers? 

Not really. While the behavior of the enemies has been made far more complex, which seems better at first, it's still not really interesting most of the time. The largest issue is that the more complex attach options for the enemies often results in awkward pairings of enemies. Two enemies attacking at the same time and being able to pass through each other with semi complicated attack options often leads to situations where avoiding one attack simply means you will almost definitely take contact damage from the other (the damage type that makes you feel stupid). There's no way to strategically deal with both at the same time, so most often you just try to aggro one away and deal with them individually, reducing the complexity of every fight as much as your can, but even with the multiple attacks many enemies now have, few are particularly interesting one on one. Hollow Knights comparably simple enemies were often full easy 1 on 1, but could create interesting dynamics when paired together or with environmental challenges. 

Speaking of environmental challenges, the main one in every biome is that you are on the ground and most of the enemies can fly. They all hover just barely in reach of a single swing at the height of your jump, and some will dodge away when possible. Will a single swing kill them or change their behavior? No, they'll be a slog, you'll need to jump and hit them multiple times, constantly, in almost every biome, throughout the entire game. And remember, jumping and attacking feel fundamentally less satisfying than in HK, and the risk of contact damage and feeling stupid are way higher. It just makes you wish you had a gun to shoot them out of the air, and when I got a tool that basically let's you delete more basic flyers, I realized how little I enjoyed engaging with any of them, and they are all over every biome, cluttering up boss runbacks, just being a pebble in a shoe that doesn't quite fit for almost every step you'll take. And their placement is consistently in places that mean you have to stop to deal with them, no matter how boring and difficult it is. Difficult because it will always require some level of coordination, but boring because it's the exact same behavior and strategy for almost all of the flying enemies. Hard and boring is a rough sell for something I'm choosing to do with my free time. Some enemy placements feel like the are suggestive of an almost "Lisa" like contempt for the player. 

People have made a lot of the difficulty and stingy economy, and while those are issues, the bigger issue to me is still the tone. Pharloom and the Citadel are both just miserable places that I don't enjoy traversing, in pursuit of a story I don't care about. I kept pushing forward hoping for bit of the Hollow Knight magic to start to sparkle again, but at 60 hours with enemies I hate dealing with, uninspiring NPCs and environments, and all of that on top of an incredibly punishing difficulty, I just don't care enough to push any further.  While it's an insane amount of content for 20 bucks, and a ton of hard work and care have clearly gone into it, I can only say that I just didn't really enjoy almost any of my time with this game.

[h1]Harsh, but not fair[/h1]

Hollow Knight was harsh but fair. Silksong is harsh and nothing else, and that difference is the whole of my complaint.

I knew what I was buying. Nobody picks up a Team Cherry Metroidvania expecting a gentle stroll. I accept the beating. What I don't accept is a beating handed out by a referee who has quietly left the building. I'm about halfway through and going for 100%, so treat this as a report from the trenches, not the summit.

[h2]The arithmetic of suffering[/h2]
Ordinary enemies hit for two masks. Not bosses, not armored brutes, but things that look like mice. Meanwhile early mice, frogs and birds take around four needle hits each, which is what genuinely dangerous enemies took in Hollow Knight. The needle upgrade arrives deep into Act One, so your damage stays stunted for hours. You hit like a wet noodle, and the noodle is fighting rodents in plate armor.

[h2]A hoarder's economy of silk[/h2]
Bind heals three masks, even midair. But when everything hits for two, you're never actually back on your feet. So you hoard silk, and the counter, needle throw and the rest of Hornet's kit sit unused. A toolkit you're afraid to use is a display case. Some stretches practically require you to cheese enemies for silk, stepping in and out of a room until the meter is full. I never once had to farm soul in Hollow Knight.

[h2]Benches, runbacks and trap benches[/h2]
In Hollow Knight, a bench ahead meant trouble was coming, and the Dreamgate covered the few brutal runbacks. Silksong has neither mercy. Benches sit far from where you die. In Sinner's Road there's a bench you have to repair by crossing a deadly gauntlet, and if you die the nearest bench is back in Greymoor. Twice I found trap benches that kill you for sitting down. Hollow Knight never pulled anything like that. A bench there was a promise of safety. Here it's a punchline.

[h2]The bosses are fine. Getting to them is not.[/h2]
The bosses are hard, about regular-Grimm hard across the board, but none I've faced has been unfair. What ruins them is the runback: a platforming section you have to clear without taking a hit, because one lost mask can decide the fight. Then a five-to-six-minute boss fight, death, and the walk again. That's not a challenge. It's a humiliation ritual. And no, runbacks don't need to "train" me. The rest of the game can do that.

[h2]Poverty as a design pillar[/h2]
Everything costs rosaries and you're always broke. In Hollow Knight, being broke was your own fault. In Silksong it's a toll booth on every road.

[h2]Sadism, itemized[/h2]
Platforming that wants near frame-perfect play. Enemies parked in your jump path so you have to eat the hit. Mount Fay's falling pillars, which you have to touch to make solid ground, with zero hint from the game. And Bilewater, which earns every bit of its reputation. I'm a player who never uses exploits or god mode, and I've had to look up guides and YouTube videos to get through sections of this game.

[h2]Pain without payoff[/h2]
Yes, Hollow Knight had the Path of Pain and the 15,000 Geo Unbreakable Strength. But that suffering was rare, optional, and paid off with a cutscene and arguably the best charm in the game. Silksong is full of mini Paths of Pain that reward you with a flea, a rosary, or some craft metal. Hollow Knight charged a lot for something great. Silksong charges a lot for pocket change.

[h2]A confession, without honor[/h2]
When I sense death coming, I now pause, quit and reload so I wake up at a bench instead of chasing my cocoon over lava or spikes. I'm not proud of it. Worse, plenty of YouTube guides from regular players tell you to save-quit at the end of long sections just to skip the walk back. In Hollow Knight, the end of a long trek gave you a shortcut. When the community's best practice is stepping outside the game to skip the game, something is wrong.

[h2]To the "get good" crowd[/h2]
Hornet being "tactical" doesn't explain why a frog needs four stabs, and "it's a different world" doesn't explain an economy built to keep you broke. Those are excuses for tuning. "Get good" isn't a rebuttal, it's declining to have the argument.

[h2]Credit where it's due[/h2]
Silksong is gorgeous, the soundtrack is incredible, the bosses are memorable, the story is good, the world feels more alive than Hallownest, and it's genuinely funny. Those things, plus my own stubbornness, are why I'm still playing. The machinery underneath is the problem.

[h2]Verdict[/h2]
Difficulty is a contract: the game gets to be hard, and you get a fair shot at winning. Hollow Knight honored it. Silksong keeps the first half.

Hollow Knight was a hike up a mountain. Hard, beautiful, and people say "I might try that someday" when you tell them. Silksong is walking barefoot on hot coals with no camera rolling, and people just ask why you'd do that.

[b]Hollow Knight I finished out of love. Silksong I'm finishing out of spite.[/b]

Honestly Disappointed
Pick a lane, do you want quick and agile combat or slow and tanky? Cause in this game you're going to get neither.

Almost everything deals 2 masks of damage, you have 5 for the vast majority of the early game so you're always 3 hits away from death.
'Oh but you can heal 3 masks' You can heal 1.5 the equivalent of hollow knight and it takes up the entirety of your silk meter. I'm sorry but you're spending more mana for less and for a game asking you to do near 10 hits just to refill a lepers hp pool isn't fun, especially when the attack patterns for most of these creatures are also pretty quick with little room for error.
Ontop of that contact damage on stunned enemies, or even if you get a parry off because you're 2 pixels in contact you take the damage anyways. Genuinely, why? I'd get if it was 1 damage on contact as a warning but 2 is ridiculous.

Fine, whatever, I'll ease up on the gas pedal and try and play slower and more meticulously.
Boss fights with ads. Why, are there so many of them? So now I'm dealing with multiple creatures (that are capable of dealing 2 masks of damage most the time) and the boss itself. So if I'm not aggressive enough the room's going to fill with ads but if I'm too aggressive I'm just getting 3 tapped? While also spending the majority of my attacks trying to gain silk to bind damage I took near 30 seconds ago and still likely being only 2 taps away from death.

You've made a beautiful, artistic world with great music and *some* fun boss designs for what I played. But for general gameplay? You've made what could've been a fast n fun experience into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slog with enemies that take forever to kill and mere seconds to put your happy little ass back on a bench. This game is a practice in poor game design and wasting ones time under the guise of 'difficulty'

I've tried quite hard to enjoy this game and just haven't been able to find it. I’m not much of a gamer. I enjoyed Hollow Knight enough to play it through on Steel Soul, but not enough to 112% it. Some will probably see this and simply think ‘Git Good,’ and that’s not entirely untrue. However, I don’t enjoy the process required, nor have the time I wish to dedicate to getting that good. 
This is my attempt to review the game fairly and share who would/wouldn't enjoy it.

There's certainly good parts that Team Cherry nailed in Silksong, as they did in Hollow Knight. I think some of the music is even better than the original. The art is higher quality (so much so I have to lower the quality settings on my computer), but still very impressive to behold. And a few mechanics provide more interesting or convenient game play (eg: hornets floating cloak, sprinting, getting Silk back when you destroy your cocoon). 


However, almost every other change I’ve found to be lateral, annoying, or clearly worse. 

I’m not personally a fan of the crest system, but I can see value in how players seeking more variety in their game play would see them as a benefit. Her twirling and weird movements at times aren’t something I’m a fan, but can see others enjoying.

Hornets ledge climbing can work both ways. The game is designed that it is required, but the automatic nature of it can become very frustrating. Combat is an obvious case for this and she may move back into the line of fire, instead of dropping safety below. There’s also a trap the game has on Mt. Fay where she’ll catch herself and climb directly into spikes. I find it infuriating when my character automatically does something no one would ever do. 
I’m not sure why they didn’t have hanging as one part, then climbing up as an action after. 

I found the reuse of bosses and attacks to be a mix of lazy and uninteresting. So far three bosses have repeated and I’m in Act 2. They’re also reused a nearly identical attack over a dozen times. 

Enemies have been a mixed bag. Some designs are simple copies of each other, other amazingly detailed units. While something that’s not wrong, but I’m not a fan of, was the incorporation of birds and mammals to the world. While they sell them as bugs, they’re clearly not. I'm not sure if it was the story telling or something else that made Bugs, fungus, plants, and spirits worked together better in my mind, but at the end of it, it's a preference thing.  

I also was disappointed by the number of bosses you fight that reward you only with access to more area. Not even new regions necessarily. Hollow knight provided a mix of charms, access, new spells and/or movement, and almost always Geo. Silksong is sparse with its material rewards. This is compounded by my personal dislike of the Crests, since they’re a reward sometimes. This obviously relates to the difficulty of the game, but I think is still a failure of the game. As if they wished to keep it comperably difficult, they could've give modest, generally ineffective rewards. Money for instance, is easy enough to come by, but would provide acknowledgement of a task completed. There's plenty of subpar trinkets in Hollow Knight. The same is true in Silksong.  


A specific failure of gameplay/story (Mild Spoilers) is with the Skull Tyrant event. I acquired wall climb, went back to the Marrows, defeated the Skull Tyrant and left to another region. When I returned to the game the next day, suddenly found myself teleported to Bone Bottom. Where I find it’s being attacked by the mini-boss I just defeated. I defeated him again. Then find a quest to go battle him for a perceived third time, which after searching discover is actually the original Skull Tyrant…...It’s clearly very easy to fix (block off access to the Skull Tyrant, wait for player to organically return to Bone Bottom, the provide access upon acceptance of the quest), so I'm judging it more harshly. 


Overall, I think other users have put it well. Silksong is a challenge. Compared to Hollow Knight it’s ratio of 'enjoyable gameplay' to 'challenge to be overcome' is heavily in the latter's favor. 

You’ll probably enjoy Silksong if you wanted a more difficult Hollow Knight or can tolerate the challenge in exchange for an expanded world.
You won’t enjoy Silksong if you wanted a game more similar to Hollow Knight, but with a new expansive lore.

Silksong o’ Silksong,
How many years I waited for thee?
Years of silence only stoked my heart.
High school, college, first job, first heartbreak. 
All passed by as I awaited that day.
But when it finally arrived, my life lay fractured before me. 
I could hear your music, but was unable to join in song.

Silksong o’ Silksong,
Elsewhile and my heart drifted elsewhere.
Other games, Other places.
Mostly disappointments, in the end. 
Cynicism crept up on me like the fog that now surrounded me.
Did I outgrow video games? 
Had I reached the end of a lifelong passion?
Had I really seen it all?
All began to blend together. 
Shoot, loot, slash, jump, level, skip skip skip skip, sprint, take the other direction because you accidentally took the main path when you were trying to find the secret area, save and quit. 
And quit I did, or so I thought.

But Silksong o’ Silksong, you pulled my heart strings like the thread at the end of a needle.
I answered pharlooms call, and what did I find?
A pilgrimage,
 Salvation,
Hope,
 Faith,
A long forgotten passion.

Silksong o’ Silksong you brought the light back to my eyes. 
The life back into this aging hollowing shell.
When hope was lost,
You did what I thought impossible.
Hollow Knight Silksong, 
 You were worth the wait.
You showed me again what video games can be.
 You made me realize I’ll never be too old for gaming if they keep making them this good. 
 Thank you team cherry.

Its been a bit over a year and I genuinely just can't reach the same high I had in this game. Don't get me wrong, I understand the difficulty curve of the game and I also found myself frustrated quite often, but I never found a game more fun in my life. The feeling of a challenge being so difficult and yet feasible added with the fast pace combat was something I never found myself experiencing until playing this game. Everyone has their take about the difficulty of the game but I honestly found it to be perfect. This game wasn't made to be played standalone. You MUST play the first game or else you are not only making it more difficult for yourself, but you also rob yourself of the experience of the first game since the second game is just that much more difficult. The simplicity of the first game made the transition to Silksong so much more fun for me. From the simple dodging of the first game because of i-frames to now needing to ACTUALLY dodge or else you WILL get hit was something that I found more fun than I thought. 

I highly recommend the game but only if 1. You finished the first game and 2. You have the patience because the learning curve really is frustrating but, personally, rewarding. This is coming from someone who's first run was done completely with the Hunter Crest though which is known to be difficult to use but I found more fun to use. If you want an easier time, try Wanderer's (it honestly makes the game so much easier) but I had more fun with the Hunter's Crest. 

The game truly is a challenge so don't play it without being prepared to suffer and sometimes go insane but if you allow the game to humble you then you'll be in for a ride. 

(But seriously I CANT FIND ANOTHER GAME THAT CAN TOP THE FEELING I HAD PLAYING THIS GAME UGH) (and to clarify I do still enjoy other games but I recently tried playing Blasphemous and I just couldn't. Highly recommend Nine Sols though. Legit the gameplay and story was so good)

Personally I am not a fan of the sequel, even though I absolutely loved the original. While the original focuses on exploration and gradual mastery, this focuses on arduous, long and repetitive combat, which feels like you are just wasting time. 

You can spend 10 minutes to reach a boss, just to die in 2 hits and do it all over again and with the narrow success margins required to finish the fight, it means repetition becomes the norm rather than the exception, making the game feel like a chore to complete. 

Overall the game is well made with beautiful graphics an interesting story and exciting mechanics, but the grind has been turned to the max, making it feel more like work, than an adventure.

Like Hollow Knight did over a year ago, Silksong has also changed my life. It is a HUGE improvement from its predecessor, from Hornet's elegant movement to the beautiful, masterfully crafted story. And while I prefer the first game way more for difficulty's sake, I still adore this game and what it's accomplished! This game is not for everyone, those who don't enjoy difficult gameplay might not have the nicest experience (I know I struggled A LOT in this game, and it put me down much more often than Hollow Knight did ;w;). However, if you love a challenge, I give this a strong recommend!

Bought when it first released, however I'll be honest I was so frustrated with the game I had to drop it for a whole year. Hallow Knight was hard but Silk Song is brutal.

Picking the game back up again after so long I had a hard time remembering things about: the storyline, areas, characters, and missions that I've already completed, which is to be expected when taking a break that long. But I loathed the idea of starting over from the intro even more just to remember everything because of my initial experience, which is a feeling I never had with Hallow Knight. I don't think I can play Silk Song without taking long breaks, so I'm just going to have fragmented experiences and memories with Silk Song and it makes me kind of sad that this is how my experience has to be so I don't fully give up on the game. 

I'd still recommend Silk Song though, because it is a very solid game. Team Cherry always delivers and have out done expectations! Visually it is beautiful, soundtrack is so atmospheric, and as someone who's always been more interested in the lore and characters of Hallow Knight rather than the boss fights, the storyline and secrets in Silk Song has a much stronger hook as it constantly keeps you curious about the world you're exploring. I will say I'm still looking for that moment where I've walked into a new area and think "this makes everything worth it" like I did in HK with the City of Tears.

Ultimately I will still keep playing Silk Song no matter how long many breaks I need, since I don't want my love for this series to end with such a bittersweet feeling.

I absolutely loved Silksong, but I am willing to admit that it is a game made for people who 112% the original Hollow Knight. As someone who really enjoys the extra mechanics for Skong and also the increased challenge, I will gladly rate it among my top 5 favorite games of all time, but second to the original HK. 

I actually put the game down at about hour 15 because I was getting bored, but once the difficulty ramped back up I was hooked. By the end you really do feel like you are playing as Hornet, the legendary older sister from Hollow Knight. 

I see a lot of rage about certain biomes on the interwebs, and honestly I think it is a bit overblown. Just take your time and engage the enemy one at a time and it is not that hard. There are some difficult 'platforming' sections, but nothing as difficult as the Path of Pain or even imo the normal white palace section of HK. 

If the runback feels too far, it probably is. Explore first, then boss. There are two exceptions. Or I was not good enough at exploring...
